title: Blackstone and Halliburton Said to Invest $1 Billion in VoltaGrid
source_used: Yahoo Finance (Power Technology article); CTV News and Axios links also found
key_facts: VoltaGrid, a US power generation company, agreed to take $1 billion in equity from funds managed by Blackstone Tactical Opportunities and from Halliburton.
The package is a $775 million primary capital raise plus a $225 million purchase of shares from existing holders.
The money is to expand on-site (behind-the-meter) power for data centers, microgrids and industrial users.

VoltaGrid also agreed to buy Propell Energy Technology, its supplier, which has about 1,000 staff in the US and Canada; two automated plants are planned in Granbury, Texas, aiming for about 300 MW per month.
VoltaGrid cites a 7.5 GW order book through 2030.
Both the investment and the acquisition were subject to customary closing conditions, with completion expected by mid-2026.
quote_evidence: US-based power generation company VoltaGrid has agreed to secure $1bn in strategic equity from funds managed by Blackstone Tactical Opportunities and Halliburton Company to fund growth.
The funding package includes a $775m primary capital raise and a $225m secondary purchase from existing stakeholders.
Both the equity investment and the acquisition remain subject to customary closing conditions, with completion anticipated by mid-2026.
why_it_matters_hint: The deal funds on-site power supply for data centers, but the coverage is from May 2026 and we could not confirm whether it has closed.
event_date: 11-12 May 2026 (Reuters, Bloomberg, Axios dated 11 May 2026; Power Technology 12 May 2026)
